input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV(I) lets Licensor unilaterally extend the Agreement for an additional seven years at its own option. Customer has no non-renewal notice window at all and would be locked into a multi-year extension it never agreed to, which is walk-away territory under this rule (automatic multi-year renewals) and fails the fallback (non-renewal window of no more than 60 days). The clause also conflicts with Article IV(II)-(III), which contemplate extension only by mutual written agreement. The shortest cure is to make renewal mutual, matching the preferred position's first limb; no price-escalation mechanic exists anywhere in the fee provisions (Article V), so no uplift cap is needed once renewal is mutual.

proposal.summary: Renewal only by mutual written agreement instead of Licensor's unilateral 7-year extension option
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option with renewal only by mutual written agreement, which aligns Article IV(I) with the mutual-extension mechanics already in Article IV(II)-(III). Our fallback is automatic 12-month renewals with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days and any uplift capped at 5%.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties.

mappings.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
